deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous folio). The function is the Euler integral I(α,β,γ,x) = ∫_0^1 y^α (1−y)^β (1−xy)^γ dy, written with a fraktur letter (𝔍, 𝔓 or S). A fourth exponent δ is fixed by α+β+γ+δ = −2, the projective-invariance condition for ∫ (z−a)^α (z−b)^β (z−c)^γ (z−d)^δ dz.
Riemann's P(λ,μ,ν,x) uses exponent differences:
• λ = α+β+1 = −(γ+δ+1)
• μ = α+γ+1 = −(β+δ+1)
• ν = α+δ+1 = −(β+γ+1)
In hypergeometric terms (my identification): I(α,β,γ,x) = B(α+1,β+1)·F(α+1, −γ; α+β+2; x). Writing a = α+1, b = −γ, c = α+β+2, the exponent differences are 1−c = −λ at 0, c−a−b = −ν at 1 and b−a = −μ at ∞.

(1) Opening remark. The connection equations of 15r (P(ν,μ,λ,1−x) expressed through P(λ,μ,ν,x) and P(−λ,−μ,ν,x), and the companion with μ,ν negated) are declared 'erschöpfend' (exhaustive). Riemann then proposes to study, for real x, the expression of P by integrals and their power-series expansions.

(2) Three real cases. The real line splits into x∈(−∞,0), x∈(0,1) and x∈(1,∞). He lists the pairs
• x/(x−1), 1/(1−x)
• x, 1−x
• 1−1/x, 1/x
My reading of their purpose: each pair maps one of the three intervals into (0,1), where the integrals are real and positive. For x<0 use x/(x−1) and 1/(1−x); for 0<x<1 use x and 1−x; for x>1 use 1−1/x and 1/x. The connection formula then gives, in each interval, a relation between functions of the corresponding pair of arguments.

(3) Eight integral representations. 'Each integral can be replaced by 7 others':
• P(λ,μ,ν,x) by the three P(λ,±μ,±ν,x);
• and by the four P(λ,±ν,±μ, x/(x−1)).
The substitution x → x/(x−1) fixes 0 and swaps 1 and ∞, hence μ↔ν.
The series interpretation:
• P(λ,−μ,ν) and P(λ,μ,ν) give the same series, by the symmetry a↔b of F.
• Likewise the pair with ν negated.
• Negating both μ and ν is Euler's transformation F(a,b;c;x) = (1−x)^{c−a−b} F(c−a,c−b;c;x).
So there are 2 distinct series in x and 2 in x/(x−1); the latter are Pfaff's transformation (1−x)^{−a} F(a,c−b;c;x/(x−1)) and its a↔b twin. These are exactly the four Kummer forms of one local solution at 0. Each form admits two Euler integrals (either numerator parameter as the 'α+1'), giving 8 integrals.
The series in x/(x−1) converge iff |x/(x−1)|<1, i.e. iff Re x < 1/2. Series in x/(x−1) and in (x−1)/x can be compared directly only where both converge, i.e. on |x/(x−1)| = 1, since otherwise one diverges when the other converges.

(4) Expanding the connection formula. The formula carried over from 15r is
I(α,δ,γ,1−x)·sin(γ+δ)π = I(α,β,γ,x)·sin βπ − I(δ,γ,β,x)·x^{δ+γ+1}·sin γπ.
Riemann now expands its right side in powers of x. Termwise integration of (1−xy)^γ gives
I(α,β,γ,x) = Σ_n Π(n−1−γ)Π(n+α)/(Πn·Π(n+α+β+1)) · x^n · Πβ/Π(−1−γ)
I(δ,γ,β,x)·x^{δ+γ+1} = Σ_n Π(n−1−β)Π(n+δ)/(Πn·Π(n+δ+γ+1)) · x^{n+δ+γ+1} · Πγ/Π(−1−β)
Here Π(s) = Γ(s+1).
To merge the prefactors (step completed on 16r, implicit here), use the reflection formula Πβ·Π(−1−β) = −π/sin βπ. Then
• sin βπ·Πβ/Π(−1−γ) = −π/(Π(−1−β)Π(−1−γ))
• −sin γπ·Πγ/Π(−1−β) = +π/(Π(−1−β)Π(−1−γ))
The last line, partly overwritten, therefore reads
I(α,δ,γ,1−x)·sin(γ+δ)π = −π/(Π(−1−γ)Π(−1−β)) · [Σ Π(n−1−γ)Π(n+α)/(ΠnΠ(n+α+β+1)) x^n − Σ Π(n−1−β)Π(n+δ)/(ΠnΠ(n+γ+δ+1)) x^{n+γ+δ+1}].
The margin factors 'sin βπ', '−sin γπ', 'Πβ' are the scratch for this combination. This is the explicit expansion near x = 0 of the Euler integral about the point 1, a form of the Gauss–Kummer connection formula. The next folio uses it to treat the degenerate case α+β+1 = m ∈ ℤ, where logarithmic and ψ terms appear.
errors: No mathematical error found. I re-derived the connection formula from the standard F(a,b;c;1−x) formula with a = −γ, b = α+1, c = α+δ+2. The coefficients reduce, via Γ(z)Γ(1−z) = π/sin πz and α+β+γ+δ = −2, exactly to sin βπ/sin(γ+δ)π and −sin γπ/sin(γ+δ)π, as written.
The series coefficients for I(α,β,γ,x) and I(δ,γ,β,x)x^{δ+γ+1} are correct.

The second 'gleiche Reihen' statement, as transcribed ('P(λ,μ,−ν,x) und P(λ,−μ,ν,x) ebenfalls'), would be wrong. Those two differ by negating both μ and ν, which is Euler's transformation (a different series times (1−x)^{c−a−b}), not the same series. The intended pair is presumably P(λ,μ,−ν,x) and P(λ,−μ,−ν,x). Either the transcription or Riemann's hand has a slip of sign.

Minor: the parenthetical 'P reell und positiv' is attached to 0<x<1. The integral ∫_0^1 y^α(1−y)^β(1−xy)^γ dy is in fact also real and positive for x<0, since then 1−xy>1. It is only for x>1 that the integrand becomes non-real. This is incomplete rather than wrong.

The statement that series in x/(x−1) and (x−1)/x can only be equated on the circle of modulus 1 is a heuristic about direct series comparison. Relations between them exist via analytic continuation (connection formulas at ∞). This is not an error in context.

results.what: Connection formula expressing the Euler integral I(α,δ,γ,1−x) as sin βπ·I(α,β,γ,x) − sin γπ·x^{δ+γ+1}·I(δ,γ,β,x), divided by sin(γ+δ)π, with α+β+γ+δ = −2
results.modern_name: Gauss–Kummer connection formula for 2F1 between z=1 and z=0 (Euler-integral form)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (1812, unpublished parts) / Kummer (1836); Riemann's P-function version in his 1857 paper

results.what: Power series of the Euler integral: ∫_0^1 y^α(1−y)^β(1−xy)^γ dy = Γ(β+1)/Γ(−γ) · Σ Γ(n−γ)Γ(n+α+1)/(n! Γ(n+α+β+2)) x^n
Each P-integral can be replaced by 7 others: P(λ,±μ,±ν,x) and P(λ,±ν,±μ,x/(x−1)), i.e. 2 series in x and 2 in x/(x−1), each with 2 integral representations
results.modern_name: Euler and Pfaff transformations; Kummer's 24 solutions (one quartet per local solution)

results.what: Pfaff-type series in x/(x−1) converge exactly for Re x < 1/2
results.modern_name: Convergence region of the Pfaff transform

results.what: Division of the real axis into (−∞,0), (0,1), (1,∞), with the argument pairs x/(x−1), 1/(1−x); x, 1−x; 1−1/x, 1/x mapping each interval into (0,1)
results.modern_name: Anharmonic (S3) group of six Möbius substitutions acting on the hypergeometric equation

deep.surprise_reason: These are working notes toward Riemann's 1857 hypergeometric paper. The material is the Euler-integral form of the Gauss–Kummer connection formula, the Euler/Pfaff/Kummer transformations and the termwise series expansion. All of it is classical and largely appears in Riemann's own published treatment. Only the details of presentation (the explicit 8-integral count, the real-interval case split) are of mild archival interest.

transcription_corrections: Last line of the main computation: the denominator 'Π(−1−γ)Π(α−β)' should read Π(−1−γ)Π(−1−β). The prefactor is −π/(Π(−1−γ)Π(−1−β)), with the struck numerator replaced by π, as confirmed on the next page.
Second 'ebenfalls' line: mathematically it should pair P(λ,μ,−ν,x) with P(λ,−μ,−ν,x), not P(λ,−μ,ν,x). Recheck the sign of ν in the image.

'findet Gleichheit für den Modul 1' is probably 'findet höchstens für den Modul 1 eine Gleichung statt' or similar: a relation between the series in x/(x−1) and (x−1)/x is possible only where |x/(x−1)| = 1.
The parenthetical reads approximately '(P reell und positiv, wenn x zwischen 0 und 1)', followed by 'Wenn x zwischen −∞ und 0:', which introduces the argument pair x/(x−1), 1/(1−x).
The margin items 'sin βπ', '− sin γπ', 'Πβ' belong to the bracketed right-hand side being assembled. They are the factors multiplying the two series before the reflection formula is applied.
